logline: A Metropolitan Police superintendent arrives in Belfast to assess a stalled murder investigation and finds herself in a methodical cat-and-mouse with a serial killer who is hiding in plain sight as a grief counsellor.

renewal.note: Three seasons aired from 2013 to 2016. Creator Allan Cubitt confirmed after Season 3 that Jamie Dornan would not return, and no further seasons were made.

bollymeter.basis: A 96 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 23 critics with consensus 'unapologetically sexy with pressure-building tension driven by plausible characters' and an 81 Metacritic score confirm Season 1 as one of the decade's finest crime dramas.

pull_quotes.text: Unapologetically sexy with pressure-building tension driven by plausible characters and motifs.

seasons.review_body: The Fall's first five episodes premiered on BBC Two and RTE One in May 2013 and generated immediate critical recognition - an 81 Metacritic score (universal acclaim) and a Guardian ranking as the tenth best television show of 2013. Creator Allan Cubitt made a structurally bold choice: showing the killer's identity from the opening episode, shifting the tension from whodunit to cat-and-mouse. Gillian Anderson's Stella Gibson - cold, brilliant, and pointedly unapologetic about her sexuality - was immediately recognised as a major television creation. Jamie Dornan's Paul Spector gave the show its unsettling centrepiece: a family man and grief counsellor whose domestic life the show rendered with eerie intimacy. The 96 percent RT score from 23 critics reflects a near-consensus that this was crime drama operating at the highest level.

episode_reviews.title: Dark Descent
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the show's structural gambit immediately - the killer's identity is no secret, and the show is not interested in the mystery of who. It is interested in the how and why, and in the parallel domestic lives of hunter and hunted. Gillian Anderson's entrance is one of the decade's great character introductions.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Stella Gibson's arrival in Belfast - her composure and authority establishing immediately that this is a different kind of detective series.

episode_reviews.title: My Troubled Cure
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 1 finale - a rare example of a season-closing episode that deepens rather than resolves. The investigation closes one chapter while opening a more complex one; the final confrontation between the two leads' parallel worlds is handled with remarkable restraint.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The closing revelation that reframes who is truly in control of the investigation.

bollymeter.basis: A 94 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 16 critics with a 91 percent audience score confirms Season 2 as a fully worthy continuation - the cat-and-mouse sustained and deepened through six episodes.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 returned in November 2014 with six episodes and a 94 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 16 critics. The season deepened the parallel structures of Season 1 while allowing the investigation to close the gap on Spector. Critics continued to praise Anderson and Dornan's performances as the central engine of the show's tension. The Edgar Award for Best Television Episode Teleplay in 2014 for Season 1 had raised the show's profile in North America, and Season 2 benefited from an expanded international audience arriving via Netflix. The 91 percent audience score confirmed the critical enthusiasm was widely shared.
seasons.season_over_season: Deepens the Season 1 cat-and-mouse with closer proximity between Stella and Spector; the tension is sustained without requiring fresh structural invention.

bollymeter.basis: A 65 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 23 critics - with the consensus 'The Fall stumbles somewhat in its third season, but still delivers enough to satisfy fans' - reflects a meaningful decline, particularly in pacing and the handling of Spector's storyline.

pull_quotes.text: The Fall stumbles somewhat in its third season, but still delivers enough to satisfy fans of the show.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 aired in September and October 2016, closing the series with six episodes that earned a 65 percent Rotten Tomatoes score from 23 critics - a significant drop from Seasons 1 and 2. The consensus noted the season 'stumbles somewhat' while maintaining enough quality for committed viewers. The narrative choices around Spector's storyline divided critics, with some finding the psychological depth earned and others finding the pacing ponderous. Anderson's performance remained above reproach throughout. Creator Allan Cubitt confirmed after broadcast that Dornan would not return, making this the definitive ending.
seasons.season_over_season: A clear step down from Seasons 1 and 2 in both pacing and critical reception; the 30-point RT drop reflects real creative difficulty in closing the Spector arc.
